source_user: A team wants lower serving cost through weight-only quantization. Define a fair comparison. Scenario variant 72: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: fix model and prompts; compare quality, memory, TTFT, TPOT, throughput, concurrency, kernel support, calibration set, and failure cases; report confidence intervals.
corrected_answer: Assumptions and controls: compare the same checkpoint, tokenizer, prompts/request trace, decoding limits, runtime and serving version, scheduler, hardware, drivers, power and thermal state. Change only weight precision; hold activation and KV-cache precision fixed. Record format, group size, scale/outlier handling, calibration-set identity and size, and every kernel or fallback. Keep calibration and held-out evaluation data disjoint. Hypothesis: at matched load, weight-only quantization lowers fully loaded cost per successful output token without breaching preregistered held-out quality, safety, correctness, or latency limits. Randomize/interleave paired baseline and quantized trials after separate warm-up, and repeat enough times to report confidence intervals. Measure quality, safety and task correctness; model and peak memory; TTFT and TPOT in ms/token; throughput in tokens/s; concurrency; utilization; error, retry, timeout and OOM rates; kernel support/fallbacks; and cleanup failures. Report median and p95/p99 with units, sample sizes and uncertainty, and separately label estimates. Include expected confounders such as batching, prompt-length mix, cache state, thermal throttling, background load, compilation and fallback. Reject the hypothesis if quality/safety/correctness or tail-latency gates fail, if fallback changes the treatment, or if cost-per-successful-token does not improve with the interval excluding the target. Canary only in an authorized disposable environment; preserve the known-good artifact, cap exposure, stop on errors or regressions, and roll back by switching the deployment and cleaning temporary artifacts.
risks: Hardware, runtime, kernel fallback, or workload changes can confound the comparison.
A synthetic calibration set may not represent production quality or safety behavior.
Cost estimates may omit host, power, storage, and failed-request costs.
evidence_required: Exact model/runtime/hardware and quantization configuration.
Disjoint calibration and held-out datasets with quality, safety, correctness, latency, resource, and failure measurements.
Repeated paired trial logs and confidence-interval calculations.
Kernel/fallback and rollback records.
